_doc: T-0826, AND THE OTHER HALF OF T-0581. Volume 1's lookup file recorded, for each of the forty-nine surnames the Newberry genealogical index (T-0570) flagged against this WORK, what volume 1 says about it — and said on itself that the Newberry cards do not record WHICH VOLUME they cite, so two ABSENT verdicts and every negative in it were findings about one book of two. This file is volume 2 looked up the same way, by the same script, so that every negative becomes a negative about the work. Each row carries its volume 1 verdict beside its volume 2 one; `work_verdict_note` below says what composing the two changed.
window_note: THE PRE-1836 WINDOW IS A FILTER AND NOT A JUDGEMENT, exactly as in volume 1. It finds lines near a printed year, which is where a compiler dates its statements. IT MISFIRES MORE OFTEN IN THIS VOLUME than in the other, and in a way worth naming: volume 2 is biographical, so a sketch that gives a birth year of 1830 puts every surname near it inside the window, and the volume's TABLE OF CONTENTS packs fifty surnames around one mention of the cholera epidemic of 1832. Three rows here (`fitch`, `herrick`, `win`) are in the window for that reason alone. Every claim was read in its own context and the window only decided what to read.
zero_result_note: A ZERO RESULT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY AN ABSENCE, because both sides of this search are OCR. Five surnames return zero here (blodget, caapbell, mattoson, morey, nlan) and the edit-distance-1 re-test splits them the same way it split volume 1's: blodget, caapbell and mattoson each stand one letter from a surname the volume does print (blodgett, campbell, matteson) and are UNRESOLVED; morey and nlan stand only beside ordinary vocabulary and are absences.
work_verdict_note: WHAT READING THE SECOND VOLUME CHANGED, which is the ticket's whole point. (1) `gunn` was ABSENT from volume 1; volume 2 prints it fourteen times, all of them Dr. Moses Gunn, born 1822 — so the surname is in the work, the negative about the TOWN survives, and it is now a negative about the work. (2) `nlan` is absent from volume 2 too, and is therefore the one lead surname of the forty-nine absent from the work ENTIRELY. (3) `gardiner` was UNRESOLVED against volume 1 because that book prints only `gardner`; volume 2 prints the card's own spelling six times, so the one-letter question was a fact about one book and the resolved answer is still a negative — Gardiner is in Moses and Kirkland and never in the early town. (4) `blodget` stays unresolved, but its near spelling now REACHES the town: Tyler K. Blodgett's brick yard of spring 1833. (5) `morey` returns zero in volume 2 and eight late hits in volume 1, so its absence is an absence from one book and the work's verdict is volume 1's. Everything else composes without surprise: nine surnames earned a claim here, and the twenty-two that are late in volume 2 are late in volume 1 too.
